What this SOP covers

This is the standard process for enrolling a client into the Elite Legal Practice (ELP) debt resolution program through Salesforce (ELP Affiliate app), from creating the Applicant record through to sending the Client Services Agreement for e-signature.

ELP is a legal service — not debt settlement ELP is an attorney-led law firm disputing debt validity under the FDCPA and FCRA. Affiliates must never market or describe the program as "debt consolidation," "debt reduction," "debt negotiation," or "debt settlement." Position it as retaining a law firm to challenge and dispute enrolled accounts. See the Compliance Script tab for the required disclosures and the full list of things affiliates cannot say.

Default assumption for this SOP

Every applicant record is created in the ELP Affiliate Salesforce app. The flow is: create the Applicant → pull a credit report → reconcile any missing debts → build the Enrollment → capture banking → send the Client Services Agreement for e-signature through Titan.

What qualifies for the program

Hard exclusions

  • Debts with original creditors — auto loans, mortgages, business loans, student loans, timeshare loans
  • Debts must be in 3rd-party collections, no exceptions
  • Most secured debts are not acceptable
  • Consolidated debt or accounts currently under representation — declined/rejected
  • Tribal loans, home improvement loans, and consolidation loans — ineligible by debt type, regardless of whether the lender appears on the unaccepted-lender list
  • GoodLeap — not accepted under any circumstance
  • Georgia, Idaho, and North Dakota — not eligible states

Acceptable with review

  • Debts already in 3rd-party collections — no exceptions
  • Department Store (or similar) credit cards — reference the debt list
  • Business debts, only in 3rd-party collections
  • Any loan tied to collateral may require additional verification even if the client states otherwise — a copy of the contract may be submitted for legal review
$250Min. monthly payment
$6,000Min. total enrolled debt
$100Min. per account (medical excluded)
49%Standard program service fee
1–72 moProgram length range

Debt list reference

The Debt List spreadsheet includes 4 reference tabs:

  • Tab 1: Debt List — general view of acceptable and unacceptable debt types
  • Tab 2: Unacceptable Creditors/Lenders — by company name
  • Tab 3: Acceptable Creditors/Lenders — by company name
  • Debt/credit type and creditor/company name are two separate checks — match creditor names one-for-one against the unacceptable list; do not lump names and types into a single check

Special account considerations

Right to Offset

The lender can take money from a bank account held with them to cover missed or overdue payments — automatically and without advance notice. Must be reviewed with the client and documented in the file (see Step 13 in Enrollment Process for exactly what to say).

Cross-Collateralization

If the client has more than one loan with the same lender, the lender can use the collateral of one loan to secure another. Paying off one loan does not release the title.

Repossession Risk

If a secured vehicle is repossessed, the client loses access to it, and if it sells for less than owed, the client may still be responsible for the remaining balance.

Required Documentation

Statements are required when credit report information is incorrect or incomplete (e.g. missing account numbers or incorrect creditor names).

Documentation

Log Special Considerations in Notes

Use the sticky Notes banner on the Applicant record for anything the next person touching the file needs to know immediately — e.g. best time to call, hearing difficulty, stated goals. Right-to-Offset, cross-collateralization, and repossession risk must always be documented here per the affiliate guidelines.

Documentation · required when it applies

Affiliate Support Ticket — Right to Offset / Cross-Collateralization

If the client has a savings or checking account at the same bank as an enrolled creditor, this step is not optional. That bank can pull funds directly from the client's deposit account to cover the enrolled debt (a "right of offset") — ELP's backend requires proof that the client was told this before enrollment, and the Affiliate Support Ticket is that proof. No ticket, no record that the disclosure happened.

What to say to the client Keep it factual and low-key — this is standard banking policy, not a knock on the program: "Quick thing I want to flag — since your [creditor] account and your checking/savings are both at [bank], that bank can legally pull funds from your account to cover a missed payment on the card. That's just how banks work, it's not specific to us. Some clients move their direct deposit to a different bank as a precaution, but that's entirely your call — I just want you going in with eyes open." Confirm they understood (a simple "does that make sense?" is enough), then log it.

Click Affiliate Support on the Applicant record, select the Confirmed Cross-Collateralization or Right to Offset template to match the scenario, and answer the "explanation provided to client (Y/N)" field honestly — this is the field ELP checks.

Affiliate Support — select Applicant and Note Template

The template pre-fills the required quick-points language (e.g. cross-collateralization: one asset secures multiple loans, paying off one loan won't release the title, falling behind puts the asset at risk). Confirm whether an explanation was provided to the client (Y/N) before clicking Next. This same step is also where you log Repossession risk or a Re-enrollment Request when those apply instead.

Send & sign

Documents & the e-signature process

What the Client Services Agreement looks like, how it gets sent through Titan, and exactly how to talk a client through signing it live on the call.

Stay on the call until it's signed Don't send the link and hang up. Clients abandon unsigned documents constantly once the call ends. Walk them through opening it and clicking every field before you say goodbye.

Script: guiding the client through signing

Once you click Send in Titan, read this to the client:

  • "You should have an email from Elite Legal Practice in the next minute or two — can you pull that up for me while we're on the phone?"
  • If it hasn't arrived after a minute or two: "Can you check your spam or junk folder for us? It'll come from Elite Legal Practice." Confirm the email address on file is correct before resending.
  • "Go ahead and open that email and click the link to review your agreement."
  • Walk them through the document screen by screen: "You'll see some highlighted fields where you need to click and sign or initial — let's go through those together."
  • For each signature/initial field: "Go ahead and click that box, then sign there," then "Click Next/Continue to move to the following page."
  • Once they reach the end: "Go ahead and click Finish/Submit to complete it." Don't end the call until they confirm they see a completion or thank-you screen.
  • Close with the Elite Legal Client Care hand-off: confirm the payment schedule and banking info one more time, then give them the Client Care number and tell them what to expect (Welcome Packet, Portal Login, Welcome Call).
If the client has trouble Most issues are the email not arriving (check spam, confirm the address) or the client trying to sign on a device that doesn't support the interaction well — suggest they switch to a phone or a different browser. Never sign on the client's behalf.

Required disclosures

Compliance script & scripting rules

ELP's legal team requests and enforces enrollment-call documentation and TCPA opt-in verification. Call recordings are mandatory upon request — if a requested call cannot be produced, the affiliate accepts indemnification responsibility for any resulting legal action.

This tab covers what you can and can't say — not how to run the call For the actual talk track and how to walk a client through the program, use the Call Flow + Scripts tab. Use this tab to check any specific line against the disclosures and restrictions below.
Position the program as… An attorney-based legal service. A process to challenge and dispute the debt's validity. A method governed by consumer protection laws (FDCPA & FCRA).
Avoid marketing or selling the program as… Debt consolidation · Debt reduction · Debt negotiation · Debt settlement

Required verbal disclosures

To ensure a well-informed client whose understanding matches the welcome-call verbiage, work these confirmations into the enrollment call:

  • Do you understand that you are retaining Elite Legal Practice, a full-service law firm, to challenge and dispute your enrolled accounts according to the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act and the Fair Credit Reporting Act?
  • Do you agree that Elite Legal Practice may contact you by email, text message, mail, or telephone moving forward?
  • Do you understand that Elite Legal Practice is not a bankruptcy law firm, credit repair company, or a debt settlement company?
  • Do you understand that payments to the program are legal service fees to represent you and challenge the validity of your debt, and are not going toward paying your debt?
  • Do you understand that Elite Legal Practice will work to redirect creditor communication and send letters of representation to help reduce calls and mail?
  • Do you understand there will most likely be a temporary negative effect on your credit, but the goal is to dispute and remove inaccurate or unverifiable information?
  • Do you understand that if you receive a summons, Elite Legal Practice will provide legal defense and attempt resolution?
  • Do you understand that communication with Elite Legal Practice is essential, including forwarding documents and documenting creditor contact?
  • Do you understand that if you bank with any enrolled creditor, it is recommended (not required) to change banks within 30 days to avoid cross-collateralization?
  • Do you understand that while attorneys may advise on settlement, this is not a debt settlement program, and no funds are held in escrow?
  • Finally, is the new payment of $____ starting on (date) affordable for you?

Things affiliates cannot say

  • Cannot promise, guarantee, or give a "most likely" outcome — every case is different and depends on individual circumstances
  • Cannot give quotes on likely reduction amounts off the balance of accounts — unless there's a defense to owing the debt (fraud, theft), there is no guaranteed reduction
  • Cannot say the firm will "wipe out the debt" or "make it like it never happened" — the firm can challenge validity and reporting accuracy, and may remove the debt and/or negotiate a settlement depending on documentation
  • There is no escrow account — client funds are never held in trust
  • The firm does not pay down the debts or toward any settlement amounts
  • Cannot tell clients they won't be sued — the firm cannot predict or control third-party actions
  • The firm does not repair credit or improve credit score/lendability — it improves the client's overall financial health
  • Cannot give estimates or specific numbers on monthly "savings," or direct clients to stop current payments
  • Cannot predict or guess the timeframe to resolve, remove, or negotiate debt — any such statement can be construed as a guarantee

Affiliate support limitations

The Affiliate Support Specialist team helps with commission questions, training resources, application support, and general affiliate-process guidance. They are not authorized to address client-specific inquiries, legal matters, or account-related concerns — including attorney communications, payment inquiries or modifications, account updates, case status requests, or other client-file matters. Warm transfer or direct these to Elite Legal for support.

Structuring the deal

Program length, fees & retention practices

Enrolling files according to this structure keeps the file qualified, affordable to the client, and competitive within the market.

Program term by debt amount

Debt AmountProgram Term
$6,000 – $10,99918 – 24 months
$11,000 – $14,99924 – 30 months
$15,000 – $24,99936 – 42 months
$25,000 – $34,99942 – 48 months
$35,000 – $44,99948 – 54 months
$50,000+54 – 60 months
All-around exception: the $250 floor, not the table, caps the term ELP will let you stretch any program up to 60 months — regardless of debt amount — as long as the client's monthly payment stays at $250 or higher. The table above is the standard guide, but the $250 payment floor is the real constraint on term length; it overrides the table whenever a longer term is needed to make a lower balance affordable. This is reflected live in the Router — check it if you're unsure how far a given file can stretch.
Maximizing file profitability Fix the program service fee at 49% to ensure maximum profitability per file, while leaving the ELP retention team room to lower the fee if the client raises affordability concerns after enrollment.

Affordability & first-draft best practices

  • Complete a thorough, honest budget analysis — the client must have sufficient cash flow after all expenses to afford the program draft amount
  • High-performing files schedule the first draft within 7–10 days of enrollment — the further out a draft is scheduled, the less likely the client is to clear it
  • Schedule drafts around the client's pay date, and use bi-weekly or bi-monthly splits to lower the per-draft amount and increase first-draft success

Retention best practices

Successful affiliates run in-house retention workflows: a next-day check-in call to address "cold feet" or post-enrollment concerns, plus a one-week and an upcoming-first-draft check-in call to see the client through to a successful first draft.

Applicant info & budgeting fields matter to underwriting

Underwriting relies on accurate expense data to validate that the program's financial structure fits the client's operational profile. Clients properly matched to the program are more likely to succeed within it — stronger retention, fewer misaligned enrollments, and less downstream friction for everyone involved. Fill out the Budget tab completely — it is not optional.

Final checklist before considering a file complete

  • Applicant record complete: personal info, address, budget, and loan information all saved.
  • Credit report pulled, and every debt the client mentioned reconciled (added via Add Missing Debt if needed).
  • All enrolled debts are in 3rd-party collections and not on the unacceptable-creditor or unacceptable-debt-type lists.
  • Program payment is $250/month minimum and total enrolled debt is $6,000 minimum.
  • Service fee set (49% standard) and program length matches the debt-amount table.
  • Right to Offset / cross-collateralization checked and, if it applies, disclosed to the client and logged via Affiliate Support — not optional when a shared bank relationship exists. Repossession risk reviewed the same way if applicable.
  • Banking information entered and read back to the client before saving.
  • Required verbal disclosures completed on the call and documented per TCPA opt-in requirements.
  • Client Services Agreement generated in Titan and sent for e-signature.
  • Client handed the Elite Legal Client Care number and told what to expect next (Welcome Packet, Portal Login, Welcome Call).
